$comment: REAL GATE for the EP packaging script — `pnpm typecheck:pack-ep`, chained
into `pnpm typecheck` and therefore into CI via .github/workflows/ci.yml.
Why a dedicated program instead of a `// @ts-check` pragma in pack-ep.mjs:
a config entry is a thing the compiler resolves, so a renamed or deleted
file becomes TS6053 and turns the gate red. A source pragma just stops
being checked the moment someone edits the line above it.
Relationship to the other two scripts programs — none of them can mask
another, because each covers a different set of files:
- tsconfig.scripts.json         include scripts/__tests__, checkJs:false.
It checks the .ts tests against the signatures pack-ep.mjs INFERs, so a
.mjs type change that breaks a test call site fails there. It does not
check the .mjs bodies at all.
- this file                     files: the two packaging scripts,
checkJs:true. It checks the .mjs bodies. It contains no tests, so it
cannot report a broken test call site.
- tsconfig.scripts-checkjs.json include scripts, checkJs:true. Backlog
only — NOT wired into `pnpm typecheck` and referenced by no CI workflow,
so it can neither enforce nor hide anything in the two above.
sign-ep.mjs is listed explicitly even though tsc pulls it into this program
anyway: pack-ep.mjs hard-imports it at scripts/pack-ep.mjs:43
(`import { signEpPackage } from './sign-ep.mjs';`), and one hard import is
enough to pull a .mjs into the program. The dependency runs that one way and
NOT the reverse: sign-ep.mjs imports only node builtins (node:crypto,
node:fs, node:path, node:url) and never references pack-ep.mjs, so nothing in
it drags pack-ep.mjs in. Naming the file means the gate's stated scope is
exactly what it checks, and dropping the import cannot silently shrink it —
checking pack-ep.mjs still checks sign-ep.mjs, precisely because the import
runs pack-ep.mjs -> sign-ep.mjs.
A NEW .mjs under scripts/ is covered by NO program (tsconfig.scripts.json
covers the .ts tests with checkJs:false and never checks a .mjs body;
tsconfig.scripts-checkjs.json is backlog only, wired into nothing). Same root
cause as the hole pack-ep.mjs had. A new script under scripts/ MUST be
added here in the same commit that creates it.
mutation-check-pane-focus.mjs is listed for that same reason, and it is the
only file here that no CI step EXECUTES: this program type-checks it, but
grep -rn mutation-check-pane-focus .github/ package.json returns nothing, so
it is run by hand. Its own header says so, gives the measured cost (16
sequential vitest runs, 78 s on an idle machine) and says why it stays out of
CI. Listing it here claims only that its lines are not unchecked, which is
what this program is for — it does not claim the harness gates anything at
runtime. Adding a CI step is a separate decision, to be made on a measurement
taken on the runner it would run on.
check-restore-block-guards.mjs is a different case from the one above: it is
wired to a gate. `pnpm typecheck` runs it first, ahead of the tsc programs,
and CI runs `pnpm typecheck` (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so a bare fs call in
the harness's finally block now fails the build. It was wired in only after
measuring the cost: 35 ms per run, of which ~23 ms is node startup. It is
listed HERE for a separate, weaker reason than the gate — this program only
claims that its lines are type-checked, which is what this program is for.
The two are not the same claim and this comment used to conflate them.
Note what this program can and cannot do: because `files` is a whitelist with
`include: []`, tsc cannot force a future .mjs under scripts/ to be added here
— a new script that is never registered type-checks at 0 errors and stays
invisible. That is a property of the whitelist design, not something this file
can fix without giving up the tight scope that makes the gate meaningful. It
also means the gate above is not self-maintaining: a new checker wired into
package.json without a tsconfig entry would still run, but be unchecked.
No compiler option is relaxed here. checkJs is on; strict,
noImplicitAny, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters and skipLibCheck all
inherit from tsconfig.json unchanged.
